nodes.label: When does an auditable, branch-preserving research process improve scientific decisions and human learning beyond polished output quality, and when does it merely add process overhead?

data.decision_owner: Researchers and research-system designers deciding how much autonomy, auditability, and human source review to require.
worlds: W1: Persistent hypotheses, evidence, failed branches, and decision reversals expose errors and improve later research decisions.
W2: Output/task quality is sufficient; extra process artifacts add documentation without changing decisions.
W3: Autonomous optimization improves task-native metrics while weakening human understanding or scientific validity outside the fixed evaluator.
data.discriminator: Compare revision-pinned research tasks with equivalent sources and budgets under output-only versus branch/evidence-preserving protocols; independent reviewers must make blinded source-grounded decisions and humans must demonstrate source-linked understanding rather than preference ratings alone.
data.falsifier: The auditable protocol does not change error detection, route decisions, source-grounded understanding, or held-out validity after controlling for time and artifact volume.
data.scope: Method-free R0 problem framing; any benchmark, replay system, or visualization is an instrument.
data.does_not_establish: Review-only source reduction; no gap, novelty, prevalence, proposal, or lifecycle transition is established.
